dedupe_keys.name: esri ireland projections of demand and bed capacity for public acute hospitals 2023 to 2040

description: This research report projects how demand for public acute hospital care in Ireland, and the bed capacity needed to meet it, could change to 2040. It was produced by the Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), led by Aoife Brick, with funding from the Department of Health, and published in May 2025 with a news summary on the ESRI site. Scenarios vary population growth, from 5.3 million in 2023 to between 5.9 and 6.3 million, the pace of healthy ageing and policy choices such as shorter inpatient stays. Projected demand rises from 1.6 million to 2.0 to 2.1 million emergency department attendances, from 4.6 million to 5.5 to 5.9 million outpatient attendances, from 1.2 million to 1.5 to 1.6 million day patient discharges, from 650,000 to 800,000 to 900,000 inpatient discharges and from 3.9 million to 5.1 to 6.0 million bed days. That implies 650 to 950 more day beds and 4,400 to 6,800 more inpatient beds, growth of 40 to 60 percent. The report is free to read online from the ESRI publications page; the ESRI states no open licence. Caveats: results are scenarios, not forecasts, and depend on migration, healthy ageing and policy assumptions. Simulation uses: demand and capacity scenarios for hospital capacity planning and system resilience models in Ireland. Related records: Eurostat hospital beds (data-eurostat-hlth-rs-bds1-hospital-beds) and the HSE urgent and emergency care report (data-hse-urgent-emergency-care-daily-report) give observed baselines.
